## TL;DR

Fixed all three linked faults for failed task cards. The card's status-line hover now carries the recorded failure detail (the same text the drawer's Waiting-for-you card shows), the yellow status line opens the panel on Status details with mouse and keyboard, and the restart confirmation is now a shared, body-teleported dialog. The old hand-rolled overlay had no `data-overlay-layer`, so while another Radix dialog was open its buttons were pointer-transparent. A regression test fails on the old structure, and a real Playwright run against the managed preview verified the tooltip, the panel click, and mouse plus keyboard use of every restart action.

## Work and rationale

The board card builds its yellow line from `needsInputHint`. That hint used the generic banner ("The agent exited with an error.") as its tooltip, while the drawer's Waiting-for-you row combines the banner with `needsInputDetail`. I reused `formatNeedsInputDetailForDisplay` so the hint prefers the concrete detail and only falls back to the banner when no detail exists. That keeps one source of truth and avoids a second copy of the reason logic.

The same hint span already had `role="button"` and keyboard handlers, but `onCardHintClick` handled only coding, PM, moving and stuck states. `tc-needs-input` fell through, so clicking the yellow line did nothing. It now opens Status details, the same destination the drawer uses for the Waiting-for-you row.

I also removed the native `title` attributes from the status hint and its detail line, moving both to the shared `data-tip` tooltip. The global tooltip already supports focus and multi-line text, so this is both styled and keyboard-visible.

The restart confirmation was the main fault. It was a hand-written fixed overlay rendered inline in the card/column/drawer tree, with no `data-overlay-layer`. Radix sets `pointer-events: none` on `<body>` while any modal dialog is open, so the overlay and its buttons lost hit-testing even though they looked correct. I replaced it with the shared `ui/dialog/*` primitives inside `<Teleport to="body">`. They stamp the layer id, trap focus, handle Escape, and make outside clicks dismiss. Restart-specific styles now decorate the shared `cc-modal` shell, so the dirty-file list and error message keep their design.

## Approaches tried

I considered adding only `data-overlay-layer` to the existing overlay, but kept the shared-dialog route because the task explicitly requires it and it also fixes the stacking-context/teleport problem in one change. For the card tooltip I considered composing banner plus detail, but chose detail-first because the acceptance criterion asks for no generic fallback when a reason exists.

For regression coverage, jsdom cannot hit-test pointer-events, so the new test asserts the two mechanics that previously failed: the confirmation is teleported out of the card and its content/scrim carry the shared layer marker. I also added tests for the detail tooltip, banner fallback, and mouse plus keyboard status-line activation.

Real-browser verification used Playwright. The declared `card:agentFailed` preview fixture seeds the failed task with a dirty worktree; `repoos shot --viewport` captured the hover tooltip, the open restart dialog, and a Cancel click that asserted the dialog count was zero. A temporary Playwright script against the managed preview intercepted `/start` and exercised Resume and Start clean with mouse clicks, plus Cancel and Resume with keyboard Enter.

## Challenges and blockers

The first `repoos shot` attempted a remote capture that timed out; forcing a local viewport capture worked. The check initially failed because an older checkpoint test still asserted the status hint's native `title` attribute. That was an intentional behavior change, so I updated the test to assert `data-tip` and the absence of `title`. I did not touch `src/server/task-watchdog.ts` or the unapproved watchdog hotfix; that approval question is unchanged.

## Key learnings

A visually correct overlay is not a clickable one: `data-overlay-layer` is part of the contract, not decoration. When a test can only prove structure in jsdom, pair it with one real Playwright run to prove the interaction. The existing shot fixture system made that cheap once the failed-card state was seeded.
